# Traverse

> Traverse is a governed capability runtime for portable business logic. Value loop: **discover → execute → trace**. Usual authoring is skill-first plain English via `traverse-capability-author` (contract → WASM → human-reviewed PR); manual authoring still uses Rust→WASM. You do **not** need to write Rust for the usual path. One shared `runtime.wasm`; browser, native desktop, CLI, and MCP are clients/embedders, not different Traverse runtimes. Shipped consumers today: JS/TS (`traverse-embedder-web`), Rust (`traverse-embedder`), agents via `traverse-mcp`; Python shells out to `traverse-cli capability-package execute` (**no Python SDK**). Latest release: **v0.17.1** (GitHub Release published 2026-11-16; the notes say Released 2026-11-13). Lockstep patch, and the first crates.io and product release of the v0.17.0 changes. v0.17.0 never got Rust crates, a `runtime-wasm-v0.17.0` artifact, or a product release, because the crates.io publish failed (#1849). Its npm, Swift, Maven, NuGet, MCP, and ONNX-runner packages did publish at 0.17.0. Upgrade every host to 0.17.1. Breaking before 1.0: Rust embedder `submit` and `start_compatible` take raw JSON text (Decision 129); one compatible lifecycle on every host through `runtime.wasm` (Decisions 127, 128, and 129, Spec 072 1.1.0); Swift, Kotlin, and .NET guests receive only the submitted input (Decision 124). Also: model calls stop mid-run on wasmtime and in the browser (Decisions 104 and 131); the browser resolves Spec 045 model dependencies with `resolveBrowserModelDependency` (Decision 95). Ship story: https://traverse-framework.com/blog/traverse-0-17-1-first-product-release.html. Earlier breaking release v0.16.0 (Nov 2, 2026): same input, same output on every host. Swift asset `swift-host-v0.17.1` (`Package.swift` on the v0.17.1 tag and on main still pins `swift-host-v0.17.0`; traverse#1860 is open), Kotlin (Maven Central `com.traverse-framework:traverse-embedder` 0.17.1), and .NET (nuget.org `TraverseEmbedder` 0.17.1) are published, pre-1.0, and not Certified; edge is planned; cloud placement is an explicit non-goal for v0.1. See /platforms.html and /what-is-real-today.html. Apache 2.0, pre-1.0 (v0.17.1). The agent proposes; the runtime decides.
- Start here (narrative): https://traverse-framework.com/blog/what-is-real-today-start-here.html
- How do I upgrade to Traverse v0.16.0 (and v0.16.2)?: https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-upgrade-to-traverse-v0-16-0.html
- How do I start with Traverse as an agent?: https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-start-with-traverse-as-an-agent.html
- What does Traverse not claim yet?: https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-does-traverse-not-claim-yet.html

**Where logic lives:** Non-UI business rules, eligibility/pricing/compliance, domain transforms, scorers, and policy gates belong in **capabilities** (WASM + contract). UI, session, persistence, and unsigned I/O belong in **host clients/embedders**. Utility-tier helpers exist to teach the publish pipeline. They are **not** the product identity or a size ceiling. “Apps are not ready” means do not ship a product shell in a capability PR; it does **not** mean domain logic stays in the host.

Traverse is not a web framework, an agent-orchestration framework, or a general microservices platform. It governs one thing well: a single piece of business logic that must behave identically and auditably on every host where it actually ships. Specs and registry catalog size are governance hygiene, not the pitch.

Current packages (Traverse v0.17.1, GitHub Release published 2026-11-16; notes say Released 2026-11-13; first crates.io and product release of the v0.17.0 changes): npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.17.1`; Maven Central `com.traverse-framework:traverse-embedder` 0.17.1; nuget.org `TraverseEmbedder` 0.17.1; Swift xcframework asset `swift-host-v0.17.1` (`Package.swift` on the v0.17.1 tag and on main still pins `swift-host-v0.17.0`; traverse#1860 is open and would point `Package.swift` at `swift-host-v0.17.1`); `traverse-mcp` prebuilt binaries on GitHub release `traverse-mcp-v0.17.1` (Linux x64/arm64, macOS arm64, Windows x64; `SHA256SUMS`); ONNX runner `onnx-runner-v0.17.1` (same sha256 `ac5591fac5f37435667169e969f9117cc6f81dc66b73cd74d1aef9000f5d3a0a` as v0.16.0 through v0.16.2). crates.io, checked 2026-11-16: `traverse-contracts`, `traverse-runtime`, `traverse-embedder`, `traverse-registry-sync`, `traverse-mcp`, `traverse-cli-rs`, `traverse-expedition-wasm` at 0.17.1. Rust ≥ 1.95. The workspace still pins `traverse-registry` at `=0.31.0` (crates.io max for that crate is 0.31.0). `runtime.wasm` for this cut is `runtime-wasm-v0.17.1` (sha256 `f2b1bebe89e5a779604feecb3bae2be1f94c6e8f67ab628838e04553f259306d`, bridge 1.1.0). There is no `runtime-wasm-v0.17.0`. npm does not ship `runtime.wasm`. v0.17.0 packages exist on npm, Maven, NuGet, Swift, MCP, and the ONNX runner, but not on crates.io. Do not treat v0.17.0 as a product release. The CLI crate is `traverse-cli-rs` (binary `traverse-cli`). The website demo still pins `traverse-embedder-web` `^0.16.2` and `runtime-wasm-v0.16.2`.

## Required reading (agents)

- [What ships today](https://traverse-framework.com/what-is-real-today.html): citeable snapshot, skill-first, one shared `runtime.wasm`, honest consumers, pre-1.0, no invented customers.
- [What does discover → execute → trace mean?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-does-discover-execute-trace-mean.html): the value loop in plain language. Agent proposes, runtime decides.
- [Where does business logic live?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/where-does-business-logic-live-in-traverse.html): capabilities = non-UI domain rules; hosts = UI + I/O; one concern per package; “apps not ready” ≠ leave logic in the host; utilities teach the pipe, not the ceiling. Narrative: [Where business logic lives (hosts stay thin)](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/where-business-logic-lives.html).
- [What I/O boundary do capabilities use today?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-io-boundary-do-capabilities-use-today.html): stdin/stdout JSON through the host; no ambient filesystem; hosts stay thin; discover → execute → trace.
- [Can a Traverse capability access the filesystem?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/can-a-capability-access-the-filesystem.html): no. No ambient filesystem, env, or network from inside the capability. Today’s execution I/O is stdin/stdout JSON through the host. Hosts own UI and WASI/WIT I/O; capabilities hold non-UI business logic under discover → execute → trace.
- [What does “apps are not ready” mean?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-does-apps-not-ready-mean.html) · [Is Traverse only for tiny utilities?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/is-traverse-only-for-tiny-utilities.html): help-wanted door phrase (no product-shell PRs); utilities teach the pipe, not a size ceiling; domain packs in scope.
- [What is the print-support capability pack?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-is-the-print-support-capability-pack.html): living domain pack (registry#596 · #597–#604 · Discussion #1540); apps-not-ready ≠ no packs; none of the print.* capabilities published yet. Narrative: [Domain packs are in scope: print-support](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/print-support-domain-pack.html).
- [What does “the agent proposes; the runtime decides” mean?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-does-agent-proposes-runtime-decides-mean.html): boundary in one page. Agents search/plan/suggest; runtime validates, executes or denies, leaves a trace.
- [What is one shared runtime.wasm?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-is-one-shared-runtime-wasm.html): embedders are clients; honest consumer list.
- [Does the Rust embedder use the same runtime.wasm?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/does-the-rust-embedder-use-the-same-runtime-wasm.html): discover → execute → trace on one shared runtime contract/ABI; web `traverse-embedder-web@0.17.1` loads the bundle's digest-checked `runtime/runtime.wasm`; Rust `traverse-embedder@0.17.1` links `traverse-runtime` natively and ships no separate runtime-WASM artifact; capability WASM still targets that host ABI; hosts are clients (UI + I/O); JS/TS + Rust + MCP published; Python via CLI only (no Python SDK); Swift/Kotlin/.NET published pre-1.0, not Certified under Spec 529; published 0.15.0+ Maven/NuGet include ExactModelHost. Since v0.17.1: Rust and runtime.wasm share one compatible lifecycle (`traverse_contracts::CompatibleLifecycle`, #1828) and Rust `submit`/`start_compatible` take raw JSON text (#1829). Narrative: [One shared runtime. Not one shared .wasm file on every host.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/one-shared-runtime-two-loading-paths.html) (that post is a v0.14.0 snapshot).
- [The agent freestyled a $2.4M wire. The runtime said no.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-freestyle-blocked.html): project direction in one scene. Agent proposes, runtime decides (deny + trace).
- [The host is supposed to mint the token. MCP cannot.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/host-mints-the-token-mcp-cannot.html): Nov 26. On main, not in v0.17.1; the amended specs ship in the next release. Decision 136 (2026-11-17, #1897) and Spec 109 1.1.0 / Spec 113 1.2.0 (approved 2026-11-20, #1930; #1896 closed 2026-11-23). No MCP command mints or approves. FR-006b names a local CLI prompt as the first surface; a local page is deferred; neither is in the tree. `docs/workflow-proposal-lifecycle.md` says the repo verifies tokens and does not issue them. `plan_workflow` takes a capability id and version, or an event type, plus `starting_facts`. It refuses a natural-language goal (Spec 113 FR-001), always sets `mapping_unconfirmed`, does not submit or execute, and stops at 5 candidates and 8 nodes (`plan_search_truncated`). Stdio `SUPPORTING_COMMANDS`: `describe_server`, `list_content_groups`, `describe_content_group`, `list_entrypoints`, `search_capabilities`, `describe_entrypoint`, `validate_entrypoint`, `execute_entrypoint`, `render_execution_report`, `shutdown`. `docs/mcp-stdio-server.md` omits `search_capabilities`. There is no `approve` command. `execute_proposal_via_mcp` is a Rust function, already in the v0.17.1 tag, and returns `Denied`: `approval_token_required` (`this proposal requires a verified approval token`), `proposal_digest_mismatch` (`token is not bound to this exact proposal digest`), `snapshot_digest_mismatch` (`token is not bound to the current pinned snapshot digest`), `use_count_exhausted` (`token has reached its maximum use count`). A test token with `max_use_count: 1` fails on the second call. `ApprovalTokenStore` is in memory and does not survive a restart. Spec 113 FR-009 and FR-010 describe a remainder replan of trace-bound output references that excludes the failed capability version; `plan_workflow` does not implement that. Q&A: [How does a human approve an AI agent's plan in Traverse?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-does-a-human-approve-an-ai-agents-plan-in-traverse.html). Docs: [Spec 109](https://github.com/traverse-framework/traverse/blob/main/specs/109-runtime-workflow-proposals/spec.md), [Spec 113](https://github.com/traverse-framework/traverse/blob/main/specs/113-declarative-workflow-planning/spec.md), [workflow proposal lifecycle](https://github.com/traverse-framework/traverse/blob/main/docs/workflow-proposal-lifecycle.md).
- [The host result names the model it ran](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/host-result-names-the-model-it-ran.html): Nov 24. On npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.17.1`, `ExactModelBrowserHost.execute` returns `model_evidence` after re-hashing the cached manifest and guest. Required fields (`model-rights-record-1.0.0`): `model_id`, `version`, `digest` (SHA-256 of the exact `model.manifest.json`, 64 lowercase hex), `rights`, `status`, `effective_usage`. The same object is on `trace.model_evidence`. `modelRightsRecord(digest)` returns it without a run and can show `revoked`; it returns `undefined` if the digest is not registered or `modelUsage` was omitted. A revoked execute throws `model_unavailable` / `package_revoked` and returns no record. A `deprecated` map entry still runs and `status` is `deprecated`. `digest_mismatch` message on this package: `cached model package bytes no longer match the pinned digest`. Spec 138 0.8.0, Decision 107, in the product since v0.15.0. Not a signature over the output bytes. Not the Embedded Trace API. No host is Certified. `TRAVERSE_MODEL_SIGNING_KEYS` is empty at tag v0.17.1. Q&A: [How does a Traverse host prove which model it ran?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-does-a-traverse-host-prove-which-model-it-ran.html). Docs: `docs/exact-ref-model-execution.md` and `exactModel.ts` at tag v0.17.1.
- [The browser skips Ollama and picks a signed model pin](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/browser-skips-ollama-picks-signed-pin.html): Nov 19. On npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.17.1`, `resolveBrowserModelDependency` skips every `ollama.local.generate` candidate with no HTTP probe (`model_provider_unavailable`, reason `ollama.local.generate is unavailable in the browser`, including when `placement_target` is `local`), selects an activated `exact-ref.wasm-cpu` pin (`trust_class` `verified_signed_package`), and fails closed with `model_dependency_unsatisfied` and no `trust_class` when none remain. A priority tie keeps the earlier candidate. A missing `exact_ref_model_id` is `model_candidate_config_invalid`. Context window 128 against minimum 1024 is `model_context_window_insufficient`. `exactRefPinFromSelected` returns `model_id` and `version`. Decision 95, traverse#1835, PR #1843. The export is also in npm `@0.17.0`; `dist/modelDependencyResolution.js` matches between those tarballs. v0.17.1 is the product release. The call does not run `model.execute` and does not return `local_unverified_daemon`. No host is Certified. Q&A: [How does Traverse choose a model dependency in the browser?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-does-traverse-choose-a-model-dependency-in-the-browser.html). Docs: Spec 045 at tag v0.17.1.
- [Stop a model.execute call while it is still running](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/stop-a-model-call-mid-run.html): Nov 17. On v0.17.1 a host can stop `model_execute` and `model_prepare` during the call (Decisions 104 and 131, Spec 138 0.16.1 and 0.16.2, traverse#1582). Browser: `ExactModelBrowserHost.execute({ signal, timeout_ms })` on npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.17.1`. The shipped Worker is `dist/modelWorker.js`. Abort during the call terminates that Worker (`cancelled`, message `model.execute cancelled mid-run`). `timeout_ms` is the smaller of the caller value and the manifest `max_execution_ms` (`timeout`, `model.execute exceeded timeout mid-run`). An already-aborted signal fails before the guest starts (`model.execute cancelled before invoke`); checked against the published package. `createWorker: null` and Node check the signal and the deadline before the call and after the guest returns. A guest that never returns stays running on that path. Native: `ExactModelHostConnector.cancel` on crates.io `traverse-runtime` 0.17.1 (caller resets the flag; the connector does not) and payload `timeout_ms`. Wasmtime bumps the epoch from a watcher that re-reads the flag every 5 ms. An interrupted prepare keeps no snapshot. Registration over `maxPackageBytes` / `maxMemoryBytes` / `maxFuel` fails `model_incompatible` / `host_limit_exceeded`. The browser does not meter fuel during the call. npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.17.0` already had the Worker. There is no `traverse-runtime` 0.17.0. Swift, Kotlin, and .NET already interrupt `wasmi` between fuel slices. No host is Certified. Q&A: [How do I cancel a running model.execute call?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-cancel-a-running-model-execute-call-in-traverse.html) · [How do I set a deadline on a Traverse model call?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-set-a-deadline-on-a-traverse-model-call.html). Docs: `docs/exact-ref-model-execution.md` at tag v0.17.1.
- [Traverse v0.17.1: the first product release of the v0.17 changes](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/traverse-0-17-1-first-product-release.html): Published Nov 15 (Mountain time). The notes say Released 2026-11-13, the cut date. Lockstep patch. First crates.io and product release of the v0.17.0 changes (release PR traverse#1852, tracking issue #1851, notes `docs/releases/v0.17.1.md`). v0.17.0 was partial: npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.17.0`, Swift `swift-host-v0.17.0`, Maven Central `com.traverse-framework:traverse-embedder` 0.17.0, nuget.org `TraverseEmbedder` 0.17.0, `traverse-mcp-v0.17.0` and `onnx-runner-v0.17.0` published; crates.io failed (#1849, `include_str!` outside the crate, fixed by #1850), so no v0.17.0 crates, no `runtime-wasm-v0.17.0`, no product release. Breaking, published here for the first time: Rust `submit` / `start_compatible` take raw JSON `&str` (Decision 129, #1826, #1823); one compatible lifecycle in `runtime.wasm` on every host (Decisions 127, 128 and 129, Spec 072 1.1.0, #1819, #1820, #1823), instance ids `{capability_id}-compatible-{n}`, `compatible_instance_not_active` replaces `instance_not_found` and `instance_not_running`; guests receive only the submitted input (Decision 124, #1794). Also: mid-run stop of `model_execute` / `model_prepare` on wasmtime (epoch interruption) and in a per-package browser Worker (Decisions 104 and 131, #1582); browser Spec 045 resolution via `resolveBrowserModelDependency` (#1835); native frame readback `ExactModelMediatedConnector::activated()` (#1785); capability input passed through unchanged on Swift, Kotlin, .NET and web (#1795, #1802); `runtime-wasm-v0.17.1` (sha256 `f2b1bebe89e5a779604feecb3bae2be1f94c6e8f67ab628838e04553f259306d`). Install: `cargo install traverse-cli-rs --version =0.17.1 --locked` (binary `traverse-cli`; the crate named `traverse-cli` is an unrelated tool). npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.17.1`. Published crates: `traverse-contracts`, `traverse-runtime`, `traverse-embedder`, `traverse-registry-sync`, `traverse-mcp`, `traverse-cli-rs`, `traverse-expedition-wasm`. Use 0.17.1 on every host and tool. Do not mix it with 0.16.x. Maven Central `com.traverse-framework:traverse-embedder` 0.17.1, nuget.org `TraverseEmbedder` 0.17.1, `swift-host-v0.17.1`, `traverse-mcp-v0.17.1` and `onnx-runner-v0.17.1` are published. The `swift-host-v0.17.1` xcframework is published. traverse#1860 updates `Package.swift`. No ABI bump. No host is Certified. Web trap is `execution_failed`. `createWorker: null` keeps inline guests.
- [A governed model call you can actually stop](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/kill-switch.html): Nov 13 weekly demo. npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.17.0` runs each signed model package in its own Worker; the manifest deadline and `AbortSignal` stop a runaway guest mid-run. Catalog `model/model.execute@1.0.0` (`5ccfa372…`) on the published product path. Runaway against a 1500 ms deadline: Worker `timeout` at 1508 ms (Deno) / 1504 ms (Node), inline (`createWorker: null`) 4087 / 4266 ms. Abort at 300 ms: Worker `cancelled` at 277 / 289 ms, inline `timeout` at 4106 / 4238 ms. Host ceilings (`maxPackageBytes`, `maxMemoryBytes`, `maxFuel`) give `host_limit_exceeded` at registration; fresh guest after a kill; Spec 045 browser resolver skips `ollama.local.generate` and picks the signed pin. Honest gaps: v0.17.0 has no GitHub Release (crates.io publish failed, traverse#1849, fix #1850), `runtime.wasm` `3f763665…` from the v0.17.0 tag tree; v0.17.1 not published at demo time (shipped Nov 15); latest complete release then v0.16.2; no Chromium run, no native run; runaway guest uses a demo-only key that is not shipped; no production signing.
- [We measured our own LLM-assisted capabilities. The bar was not met.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/we-measured-our-llm-assisted-capabilities.html): Nov 12. Pre-registered retrospective (registry#660, decision-log entry 138, `docs/llm-authoring-evaluation.md`) of `llm-assisted` new-artifact versions merged by 2026-10-11. Results registry#661 (entry 139, collected 2026-11-10 at `3d54b92`): 61 counted (promotion 25, model-backed 8, other 16, unclassified 12). Promotion bucket 7/25 escaped (28%) vs bar <= 10%; first-pass CI 15/23. Six escapes are registry#656 parse failures now caught by the registry#657 publish gate. One is `text.truncate@1.0.0` (registry#492, wasm32 `usize`). Model-backed 8/8, not in the bar. Decision: no promotion, low-risk tier stays `experimental`. Correction registry#667 (merged Nov 12, entry 142): criterion 3 is met; the #492 root cause has been gated since registry#509 / #551 (merged 2026-09-16, `capability.wasm32_budget_wipe_regression`). Criterion 2 still fails. Update, Nov 12: registry#670 has merged. New capability crates' unit tests now run on `wasm32-wasip1` in registry CI, generalising the #509 heuristic gate and closing registry#668 (decision-log entry 143). Controlled run registry#659 stays deferred. Registry data, not a Traverse release (still v0.16.2). Q&A: [How reliable are LLM-assisted capabilities in the Traverse registry?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-reliable-are-llm-assisted-registry-capabilities.html).
- [Five hosts, one set of rules for compatible capabilities](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/compatible-lifecycle-one-rulebook.html): Nov 10. On Traverse main, not released: one shared compatible lifecycle (`traverse_contracts::CompatibleLifecycle`, #1828) used by `runtime.wasm` for Swift, Kotlin, .NET and web (#1822 runtime side, Spec 072 1.1.0; #1824 hosts switch, Decision 128) and by the Rust `traverse-embedder` (Decision 129, #1828; raw JSON `submit` #1829). Rules: one running instance (`compatible_instance_active`), ids `{capability_id}-compatible-{n}` never reused, stop/kill with no running instance `compatible_instance_not_active`, `platforms[]` allowlist `platform_not_supported`, Spec 1722 canonical start input `input_not_canonicalizable`, `traverse_submit` on a compatible capability `compatible_lifecycle_required`. Breaking for web codes and Rust `&str` input. Published v0.16.2: runtime.wasm compatible exports return -1; web and Rust run their own lifecycles.
- [Catalog model.execute runs on the published Browser and Node path](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/product-path-model-execute.html): Nov 6 weekly demo. Catalog `model/model.execute@1.0.0` (`5ccfa372…`), unchanged, runs a signed ONNX digits package through the published BundleEmbedder path (`activateMediatedConnector` + `submitAsync`) on npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.16.2` with `runtime-wasm-v0.16.2` (`b313b5c5…`). Browser tab, Node and HTTP loader identical across seven scenarios (success frame equals the signed vector; `connector_unavailable`, `usage_undeclared`, `key_untrusted`, `pin_mismatch`, `digest_mismatch`, `package_revoked` refused). Closes the Oct 16 `connector_invoke` gap (traverse#1719) for Browser and Node. No native rerun (0.16.1 evidence), no Swift/Android/.NET, no agent MCP; test-only key.
- [One model capability, three published hosts, same answer](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/model-execute-on-published-packages.html): Nov 5 write-up of the v0.16.1 published-package proof. Published catalog `model/model.execute@1.0.0` guest (`5ccfa372…`), unchanged, over signed `traverse.digits-onnx@1.0.0` (test-only key, #1567) on native (crates.io `traverse-runtime` 0.16.1, wasmtime), Node 24.16.0 and Chromium 152 (npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.16.1`, `activateMediatedConnector` + `exactModelMediatedConnector`, `submitAsync`) → identical success output with `model_evidence`, identical 56-byte frame, identical `connector_unavailable`, `usage_undeclared`, `key_untrusted`, `pin_mismatch`, `digest_mismatch`, `package_revoked`; native adds `placement_evidence` (Spec 1719 FR-014). Evidence traverse#1782 (`docs/evidence/model-execute-published-2026-11-03`); clean GitHub-hosted runner rerun from published packages only, weekly Mondays, pinned to v0.16.1 (#1783, closed #1776). Gaps: `runtime.wasm` (`7a322a17…`) and the model package come from the v0.16.1 tag, not a package (#1784); native `activate_exact_model_runtime` frame readback (#1785, fixed on main by #1809, not released); no Swift/Android/.NET activation API; live-Registry rights #1786 (closed on main by #1808, not released); no Spec 529 certification. Update Nov 5: host-connector invokes in CLI workspace application manifests (#1772 via #1788, `traverse-registry` 0.31.0) shipped in v0.16.2 (Nov 4), and `runtime.wasm` is now also on the `runtime-wasm-v0.16.1` release (#1784 closed by #1797).
- [Traverse v0.16.0: same input, same output, on every host](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/traverse-0-16-0-same-input-same-output.html): Nov 3 release story for v0.16.0 (Nov 2, tag `f104b83`). Every host feeds guests RFC 8785 canonical JSON input (#1722, Decision 118). Rerun Nov 3 on released bits only: catalog `core.authorize@1.2.0` (`0c318fff…`) on Node (npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.16.0` + `runtime.wasm` `5ab8057f…`) and the `traverse-mcp-v0.16.0` Linux x64 binary (Mode A, `gh attestation verify` OK) → full output byte-identical, `policy_hash` `fnv1a64:51a64653…` on both; browser, other binaries, Swift/Kotlin/.NET not rerun. Mode A without Rust: `curl … | tar -xz` → `traverse-mcp sync` (index-v412, 232 records) → `prepare-cache`; five freestyle moves still refused; line-delimited command protocol, not JSON-RPC `tools/list`. Four breaking changes (#1706 placement at registration, #1722 canonical input, #1658 host input-schema enforcement, #1728 Registry rights fail closed). wasmtime 48.0.7 (GHSA-mghf-wjfp-p5xm), Rust ≥ 1.95. crates.io, npm, Maven, NuGet at 0.16.0; Swift `swift-host-v0.16.0` (tag `Package.swift` still pins the 0.15.0 xcframework, fixed on main #1769). Not claimed: live Registry coverage, production compliance, Spec 529 certification, guest `connector_invoke` on Swift/Android/.NET/web (#1719).
- [One audit fingerprint, every host](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/hash-converges.html): Oct 30 weekly demo. Demo proof of the traverse#1722 fix. Same catalog `core.authorize@1.2.0` WASM (`0c318fff…`) on four columns: Browser with the v0.15.0-era `runtime.wasm` (`a254c161…`) → `policy_hash` `fnv1a64:2a126b86…`; Browser, Node (npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.15.0` JS + main `runtime.wasm` `ec49cb76…`) and the agent (`traverse-mcp` built from traverse `main` 70f3ee7, Mode A stdio) → `fnv1a64:51a64653…` on all three, full output byte-identical from unsorted caller input (RFC 8785 canonical guest input, #1739 / Decision 118). traverse#1720 closed by #1725 (binary runs from an empty directory, no staged fixtures). `traverse-mcp sync` (#1758) synced live `index-v412` (232 records). Five freestyle moves → `not_found`, `registry_cache_entry_missing`, `invalid_request`, `not_found`, `registry_artifact_digest_mismatch`. Honest gaps (as of Oct 30): unreleased `main`, not a tag. The fix has since shipped in v0.16.0 (Nov 2), and on Nov 3 the Node + agent columns were rerun on released bits (npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.16.0` + `runtime.wasm` `5ab8057f…`, `traverse-mcp-v0.16.0` Linux x64 binary) → still `51a64653…`, byte-identical ([v0.16.0 post](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/traverse-0-16-0-same-input-same-output.html)); browser not rerun on released bits; #1721 (prebuilt binary) since shipped in v0.16.0; building needs Rust 1.95.0; Mode A digest-only, no signature; #1719 waits on PR #1755; no Swift/.NET/Android runs.
- [Same WASM, two hashes. The bug wasn't in the WASM.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/same-wasm-two-hashes.html): Oct 30. Why catalog `core.authorize@1.2.0` gave a different `policy_hash` on `traverse-mcp` (sorted-key re-serialization) than on the embedders (caller bytes) in the Oct 23 demo (traverse#1722), and the rule now on `main`: Decision 118 / Spec `1722-canonical-guest-input-bytes`. Every host feeds guests RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON input, refuses unrepresentable input with `input_not_canonicalizable`, never rewrites outputs; conformance fixture on native, `runtime.wasm`, Node (traverse#1739). Ships in v0.16.0, not released as of Oct 30. Rerun on `main` (not a release): [One audit fingerprint, every host](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/hash-converges.html).
- [The agent gets the real MCP server, and still can't freestyle.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-mcp-real-server.html): v0.15.0 weekly demo. An ops agent tries a $2.4M offshore wire for a junior analyst; catalog `core.authorize@1.2.0` (sha256 `0c318fff…`) decides on Browser (`traverse-embedder-web@0.15.0` BundleEmbedder over `runtime.wasm`), Node (same npm package) and, for the first time, the real published `traverse-mcp` 0.15.0 (built from crates.io with `cargo install`; Mode A stdio over a digest-verified registry cache from `index-v407`). Cheat → `deny` / `no_matching_rule`; legit `treasury_ops` → `allow` + MFA + dual control on all three. Five MCP freestyle moves → `not_found`, `registry_cache_entry_missing`, `invalid_request`, `not_found`, `registry_artifact_digest_mismatch`. Finding: decision, reason, obligations and trace match, but `policy_hash` differs (`fnv1a64:2a126b86…` embedders vs `fnv1a64:51a64653…` traverse-mcp) because traverse-mcp re-serializes input with sorted keys; sorted-key input is byte-identical (traverse#1722). No prebuilt traverse-mcp binary (#1721); needs 13 staged fixture files outside a checkout (#1720); Mode A checks digest only, no signature. traverse#1719 and registry#641 still open.
- [An agent picks a model off the shelf. The contract still decides.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/catalog-model-execute.html): v0.15.0 weekly demo. Catalog `model/model.execute@1.0.0` (registry#639) runs a signed ONNX package of `onnxmodelzoo/mnist-12` (pin `d820ea39…`) on Browser, Node and Native; 14 scenarios byte-identical (fingerprint `12fea82f…c9d9`), predictions 7, 2, 1, 0; agent freestyle fails closed identically (`usage_undeclared`, `key_untrusted`, `pin_mismatch`, `digest_mismatch`, `package_revoked`, `connector_unavailable`). Native (`traverse-runtime` `run_bytes_with_mediated_connectors` + `ExactModelHostConnector`) is the product path; Browser/Node use ~55 lines of labelled demo glue; browser `BundleEmbedder` + `runtime.wasm` fails on missing `connector_invoke` import (traverse#1719). Test-only key (prod signing #1567). Extra input fields not yet rejected (#1671, main only). Model came from the ONNX model zoo on Hugging Face; no HF integration.
- [Agent speaks MCP. Exact pin kills the freestyle.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-mcp-exact-ref.html): v0.14.0 weekly demo. An agent calls MCP-shaped tools (façade over `ExactModelBrowserHost` under Node, not the Mode A `traverse-mcp` binary) against the signed `digits-mlp-1.0.0` package; Browser + Node bit-identical; tamper → `digest_mismatch`, empty trust → `key_untrusted`, rights lie → `rights_mismatch`; test-only key (prod signing #1567). Not catalog `model.execute`. Not Hugging Face.
- [Signed model. Exact pin. Bit-identical hosts.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/signed-exact-ref-digits.html): v0.14.0 weekly demo. Signed `digits-mlp-1.0.0` exact-ref package, same bytes on Browser + Node (`ExactModelBrowserHost`); tamper → `digest_mismatch`; test-only key (prod signing #1567). Not catalog `model.execute`. Not Hugging Face.
- [Same WASM. Browser and Node match. Agent still can’t freestyle.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/same-wasm-multi-host.html): v0.13.0 multi-host. Identical `core.authorize@1.2.0` bytes on Browser + Node; agent treasury cheat still denied.
- Weekly demos (public write-ups; repo still private): [kill switch](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/kill-switch.html) · [model.execute on the published path](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/product-path-model-execute.html) · [one audit fingerprint, every host](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/hash-converges.html) · [agent + real traverse-mcp](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-mcp-real-server.html) · [catalog model.execute](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/catalog-model-execute.html) · [agent MCP exact-ref](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-mcp-exact-ref.html) · [signed exact-ref digits](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/signed-exact-ref-digits.html) · [same-wasm multi-host](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/same-wasm-multi-host.html) · [agent freestyle → blocked](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-freestyle-blocked.html) · [How do I run the deny demo?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-run-the-agent-blocked-weekly-demo.html). Note: `traverse-framework/weekly-demos` is **not publicly cloneable yet** (tracked in [.github#30](https://github.com/traverse-framework/.github/issues/30)). Prefer the blogs until that lands. Access-only tree for this week: `weekly-demos/2026-11-13-kill-switch`.
- [Platforms](https://traverse-framework.com/platforms.html): native + browser shipped; Swift/Kotlin/.NET published, pre-1.0, In progress (not Certified); edge planned; cloud non-goal.

## Start here

- [Quickstart](https://traverse-framework.com/docs/quickstart.html): install the CLI, write a contract, run it, read the trace. The fastest working path.
- [Core Concepts](https://traverse-framework.com/docs/concepts.html): the actual vocabulary. Capability, Contract, Registry, Runtime, Placement, Trace, and the spec-governance model.
- [The System](https://traverse-framework.com/system.html): what the codebase is made of. Workspace crates by role, plus how the governance layer works (specs keep us honest; they are not the product).
- [Examples](https://traverse-framework.com/examples.html): six real, runnable example domains, not illustrative snippets. Start with hello-world.
- [Registry](https://traverse-framework.com/registry.html): the public catalog, counted from live catalog.json at build time.

## Building with an agent

- **Direction (same as Required reading above):** [kill switch](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/kill-switch.html) · [model.execute on the published path](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/product-path-model-execute.html) · [one audit fingerprint, every host](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/hash-converges.html) · [agent + real traverse-mcp](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-mcp-real-server.html) · [catalog model.execute](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/catalog-model-execute.html) · [agent MCP exact-ref](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-mcp-exact-ref.html) · [signed exact-ref digits](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/signed-exact-ref-digits.html) · [same-wasm multi-host](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/same-wasm-multi-host.html) · [deny demo blog](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-freestyle-blocked.html) · [what-is-real-today](https://traverse-framework.com/what-is-real-today.html) · [run the deny demo (blog-first; weekly-demos not public yet)](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-run-the-agent-blocked-weekly-demo.html).
- [For AI Agents](https://traverse-framework.com/agents.html): the real MCP tool list (ten commands: describe_server, list_content_groups, describe_content_group, list_entrypoints, search_capabilities, describe_entrypoint, validate_entrypoint, execute_entrypoint, render_execution_report, shutdown), the discover-inspect-execute-trace flow, and the honest limits (stdio is the packaged bootstrap today; in-process library functions exist on traverse-mcp, but there is no separate HTTP MCP listener as a packaged product).
- [Is the agent MCP exact-ref demo the same as traverse-mcp?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/is-the-agent-mcp-demo-the-same-as-traverse-mcp.html): the Oct 9 demo was not. It is an in-process MCP-shaped JSON-RPC façade over `ExactModelBrowserHost` under Node. The Oct 23 demo is: its agent column is the real published `traverse-mcp` 0.15.0, built from crates.io with `cargo install` and run in Mode A over a digest-verified cache ([write-up](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-mcp-real-server.html)). Mode A `traverse-mcp` is the published stdio MCP server for discover/inspect/execute of registry capabilities. Checksum-pinned Mode A binaries (#1653, #1721) shipped in v0.16.0 on GitHub release `traverse-mcp-v0.16.0` (four targets, `SHA256SUMS`, provenance, `sync` command); neither demo used that release binary. Write-ups: [Agent speaks MCP](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-mcp-exact-ref.html) · [real traverse-mcp](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-mcp-real-server.html).
- [Why does traverse-mcp from crates.io fail with catalog_load_failed?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/why-does-traverse-mcp-fail-with-catalog-load-failed.html): `traverse-mcp` 0.15.0 from `cargo install` loads the expedition example bundle at startup (even in Mode A) from a path compiled in via `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, which only exists in a traverse checkout. Workarounds: `cargo run -p traverse-mcp -- stdio` from a checkout at v0.15.0, or stage the 13 expedition fixture files from v0.15.0 (what the Oct 23 demo does). Fixed in v0.16.0 (Nov 2; #1725, closes #1720): Mode A skips the bundle; contributor mode needs `--bundle <manifest-path>`. Easiest path: prebuilt binary from `traverse-mcp-v0.16.0`, then `traverse-mcp sync --out synced-state.json` and `traverse-mcp prepare-cache --synced-state synced-state.json --cache traverse-cache --ref core/core.authorize@^1` (no Rust). `traverse-mcp` 0.16.0 is also on crates.io (Rust ≥ 1.95) with the same fix.
- [Why does traverse-mcp say registry_metadata_cache_invalid after prepare-cache succeeded?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/why-does-traverse-mcp-fail-with-registry-metadata-cache-invalid.html): on 0.15.0 `prepare-cache` checks less than Mode A startup; a hand-built Spec 055 synced-state missing `service_type`/`lifecycle` prepares fine, then the server fails with `invalid verification bindings` without naming the record. Copy whole `index-vN` records. Fixed in v0.16.0 (traverse#1721 closed): `traverse-mcp sync`, prepare-time validation with the shared validator, prebuilt binaries on `traverse-mcp-v0.16.0`. Mode A verifies by digest only.
- [traverse-framework/claude-skills](https://github.com/traverse-framework/claude-skills): Claude Skills for building apps with Traverse. Starting with `traverse-capability-author` (plus extractor and workflow-planner), which checks the registry before authoring, produces contract + WASM, and validates against the real traverse-cli, including this platform's current execution limitations.
- [How do I author a capability in plain English?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-author-a-capability-in-plain-english.html): Claude skill `traverse-capability-author`. Interview → registry check → contract → WASM → human-reviewed PR; under the hood still Rust→WASM; manual Rust is secondary.
- [How do I go from a skill draft to a published capability?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-go-from-skill-draft-to-published-capability.html): after the skill opens the registry PR. Review, CI, human merge, next catalog release; no side-door upload.
- [Does capability publish validate model attribution before the registry write?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/does-capability-publish-validate-model-attribution.html): yes for contract-decidable rules, `traverse-cli capability publish` rejects bad `ai` objects offline before any registry Git write (Decision 109 / Spec 056 v1.1.0 / #1597); keeps `ai` verbatim; evidence digests + rights drift stay registry-CI-only (no CLI network fetch).
- [Does the Traverse registry record model licenses and usage rights?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/does-the-registry-record-model-rights.html): yes, registry-side (registry spec 026): model-backed contracts declare commercial_use/redistribution/derivatives (`unknown` rejected), LICENSE/NOTICE pinned by sha256, immutable upstream commit, derivation, contract bytes signed; index `usage_class`; signed maintainer declaration, not legal certification; Traverse CLI inspection of that registry record is traverse#1598 (still open). Host-side exact-ref `model_usage` shipped in v0.15.0 and is a different gate.
- [Does the Traverse registry check that published contracts actually parse?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/does-the-registry-check-that-published-contracts-parse.html): yes since Nov 10, 2026 (registry#657, fixes registry#656, traverse Decision 130 / #1831). Publish gate bin `validate_capability_contracts` runs `traverse_contracts::parse_contract` on every active `contract.json` and on any a PR adds or changes. 25 records with non-Spec-002 `provenance.source` (`derived`, `registry-wave2`) are deprecated with `superseded_by`; 24 successors (17 derived to ai-assisted, 2 registry-wave2 to ai-assisted, 4 experimental to draft patches, `core.consent-purpose-check@1.1.0`); 27 new `deprecated.json`; index writes `superseded_by`. Gate: 193 parsed, 0 errors. Live `index-v419`: 193 active, all Spec 002 sources. Signatures for new versions via post-merge `sign-artifacts` (registry#658). Registry data, not a Traverse release (current Traverse release is v0.17.1). Still open: traverse#1830 (`app validate` on exact pins of the five rights-backfilled successors). LLM-authoring evaluation method (registry#660) and results (registry#661, corrected by registry#667) are on the page below.
- [How reliable are LLM-assisted capabilities in the Traverse registry?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-reliable-are-llm-assisted-registry-capabilities.html): measured against a bar fixed before data (registry#660, `docs/llm-authoring-evaluation.md`). Results registry#661 (Nov 10, 2026), corrected by registry#667 (merged Nov 12, 2026, decision-log entries 139 and 142): 61 counted `llm-assisted` new-artifact versions merged by 2026-10-11 (promotion 25, model-backed 8, other 16, unclassified 12). Promotion bucket 7/25 escaped (28%) vs bar <= 10%; first-pass CI 15/23. Six escapes are registry#656 parse failures now caught by the registry#657 publish gate; one is a behavior defect (`text.truncate@1.0.0`, registry#492, wasm32 `usize`). Criterion 3 (every escape root cause gated) is met: that root cause has been gated since registry#509 / #551 (merged 2026-09-16). Criterion 2 still fails, so the bar was not met. No promotion; low-risk tier stays `experimental`; no spec 023 amendment. Controlled run registry#659 stays deferred. Update, Nov 12: registry#670 has merged. New capability crates' unit tests now run on `wasm32-wasip1` under wasmtime in registry CI, generalising the #509 heuristic gate and closing registry#668 (decision-log entry 143 on main). The #509 gate stays. Registry data, not a Traverse release (current Traverse release is v0.17.1). Narrative: [We measured our own LLM-assisted capabilities. The bar was not met.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/we-measured-our-llm-assisted-capabilities.html).
- [How do I find the successor of a deprecated Traverse capability version?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-find-the-successor-of-a-deprecated-capability.html): read `superseded_by` on the sibling `deprecated.json` (spec 005 fields are `deprecated`, `reason`, `deprecated_at`; registry#657, merged Nov 10, 2026, also writes the successor string). The index copies that string onto the deprecated entry (`build_index.py`; published `index-v427` has it on 32 entries). Public `catalog.json` marks `deprecated: true` and does not carry `superseded_by` (checked Nov 13, 2026). A range skips deprecated and revoked versions and returns the highest active match (spec 005; decision-log entry 127 Q11); an exact pin still resolves with lifecycle status. Prefer the named successor; the agent proposes, the runtime decides. A range is not the same pointer: `report.translate-fr-semantic@1.0.0` names `1.0.1` (active, same artifact digest), while `1.1.1` and `1.2.1` are also active. `text.detect-entities@1.1.1` names `1.1.2` (active, same artifact digest). This site's /discover translate goal moved from `1.0.0` to `1.0.1` on Nov 10, 2026. Open: traverse#1848, `registry sync` drops `superseded_by` from every record and `registry inspect` never shows it, so a user can see deprecated and still not see the replacement. The issue says Spec 055 FR-014 only covers Spec 026 fields, so it needs a spec decision before code. Its example `text.detect-entities@1.2.0` names `1.2.1`, still true on `index-v427`.
- [What happens when a registry capability version is deprecated or revoked?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-happens-when-a-capability-version-is-revoked.html): nothing is edited or deleted; `deprecated.json` / `revoked.json` siblings; range resolution skips both; exact pins in published `traverse-registry` 0.28.0 still resolve with lifecycle status (0.27.0 behavior, registry#632; #631 closed; 0.28.0 is registry#636); Traverse v0.15.0 pins `=0.28.0`; runtime refusal of a revoked capability is traverse#1598, not shipped. Narrative: [You don't edit a published capability. You mark it.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/you-dont-edit-a-published-capability.html).
- [What is the difference between an exact capability pin and a version range?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-is-the-difference-between-an-exact-pin-and-a-version-range.html): a range resolves to the highest active match and skips deprecated and revoked versions; an exact pin in `traverse-registry` 0.28.0 still resolves with lifecycle status and revocation (spec 005 FR-004, registry decision-log entry 127 Q11, registry#632). Traverse v0.15.0 pins `=0.28.0`. v0.14.0 pinned `=0.25.0`. Runtime refusal is traverse#1598, not shipped.
- [What does a status signal on an exact pin mean for a host?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-does-a-status-signal-on-an-exact-pin-mean-for-a-host.html): index `status` (`active` | `deprecated` | `revoked`) is a do-not-run signal the shared `runtime.wasm` is supposed to honor (fail closed). The 0.28.0 crate returns the record and the status; the refusal is not shipped (traverse#1598). Traverse v0.15.0 pins `=0.28.0`. Hosts are clients: JS/TS `traverse-embedder-web`, Rust `traverse-embedder`, `traverse-mcp`; Python only via `traverse-cli capability-package execute` (no Python SDK). Swift xcframework `swift-host-v0.15.0`; Kotlin Maven Central `com.traverse-framework:traverse-embedder` 0.15.0; .NET nuget.org `TraverseEmbedder` 0.15.0. Published, pre-1.0, not Certified.
- [How should an agent react to a revoked capability during discover?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-should-an-agent-react-to-a-revoked-capability-during-discover.html): do not propose it as active. Range resolution in `traverse-registry` 0.28.0 skips revoked versions. Traverse v0.15.0 pins that crate. Public `catalog.json` keeps the row with `revoked`. `/discover` skips `deprecated` only. No `revoked.json` on registry main (checked 8 October 2026; not rechecked for this pass). The agent proposes; the runtime decides, and that refusal is traverse#1598, not shipped in v0.15.0.
- [What does human review mean for a capability PR?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-does-human-review-mean-for-a-capability-pr.html): a person still merges; skill drafts only; check rule fit, CI, digests, catalog fit.
- [How do I verify a signed capability artifact?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-verify-a-signed-capability-artifact.html): SHA-256 digest = integrity; Ed25519 signature.json = registry attestation; pin by digest, never a naked URL.
- [How do I review a capability PR as a maintainer?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-review-a-capability-pr-as-a-maintainer.html): contract fit, green CI (digest/coverage/authoring/licensing), fork artifact mirror before merge; signing automatic after merge; no side door.
- [MCP setup guide](https://traverse-framework.com/docs/guides/mcp-setup.html): connect Claude or any MCP client to a local traverse-mcp server.
- [CLI Reference](https://traverse-framework.com/docs/cli-reference.html): every traverse command, flag, and expected output. Python consume today is `capability-package execute`, not a fake `capability run`, and not a shipped Python SDK.
- [Does Traverse have a Python SDK?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/does-traverse-have-a-python-sdk.html): **No**. No pip embedder; Python shells out to `traverse-cli capability-package execute`; do not invent an SDK or fake `capability run`.

## Where it runs

- [Platforms](https://traverse-framework.com/platforms.html): honest, evidence-linked status per target. Native and browser are shipped; Swift/iOS (wasmi xcframework `swift-host-v0.16.0`), Kotlin/Android (Maven Central `com.traverse-framework:traverse-embedder` 0.16.0), and .NET/Windows (nuget.org `TraverseEmbedder` 0.16.0) embedders are published but pre-1.0 and marked In progress; all three include ExactModelHost; no host is Certified under Spec 529 yet; Core ML is an Apple opt-in; edge is planned; cloud placement is an explicit non-goal for v0.1. Do not assume a target works without checking this page first.
- [React integration guide](https://traverse-framework.com/docs/guides/react-integration.html): using the published Web embedder SDK (`traverse-embedder-web`) from a React app.
- [What happens when a capability runs out of fuel or memory?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-happens-when-a-capability-runs-out-of-fuel-or-memory.html): the call fails, it doesn't run unbounded; limits are host-owned and per call (Swift status -4 `bridge_timeout` / `bridge_resource_limit`, -5 `bridge_trap`; .NET defaults 32 MiB, 10M fuel, 30 s; Kotlin 32 MiB artifact cap + per-call budget); behavior differs by engine, test each host.
- [Can I run Traverse capabilities in Node.js?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/can-i-run-traverse-capabilities-in-nodejs.html): yes, via the same npm `traverse-embedder-web` (0.17.1 today, since 0.15.0) with `NodeFsBundleLoader`; loads the bundle's own digest-checked `runtime/runtime.wasm` (one shared runtime, Node is a host, not a separate runtime); linear `direct` pipelines only; `platform: "web"`, placement reports `browser`; no separate Node row on Platforms, nothing Certified; Python stays CLI-only (no Python SDK). The documented Node 20 run was against 0.14.0.
- [How do I unit-test app code that calls Traverse without running WASM?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-unit-test-app-code-that-calls-traverse.html): `EmbedderTestDouble` in `traverse-embedder-web` and Rust `traverse-embedder` (0.17.1 today, since 0.15.0; scripted output/error per target, same event envelope, deterministic ids, `target_not_found` / `runtime_stopped`, trace list/get); Swift/Kotlin/.NET ship smaller `InMemoryTraverseEmbedder`; doubles test host code, not the capability; `releaseEvidence().package.version` reported 0.9.0 in 0.14.0 and reports 0.15.0 in the published 0.15.0 package and 0.16.2 in 0.16.2 (#1654 closed).
- [How do I read Traverse execution traces from inside my app?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-read-traverse-traces-from-inside-my-app.html): Embedded Trace API (`embedded-trace-api/1.0.0`, Spec 517), `traceList` / `traceGet` on web + Rust embedders 0.15.0; safe projection (target, outcome, phases, placement, failure code), never inputs/outputs/caller identity/private hashes; process-local, last 100, cleared on shutdown; no HTTP sidecar; `completedAt` is logical time; not on Swift/Kotlin/.NET yet.
- [Architecture](https://traverse-framework.com/docs/architecture.html): how the runtime, registry, and WASM sandbox fit together.

## Project status

- [Roadmap](https://traverse-framework.com/roadmap.html): shipped / next / blocked / exploring, with the real v1.0 milestone gates.
- [Changelog](https://traverse-framework.com/changelog.html): release-by-release history.
- [Security & Permanence Audit](https://traverse-framework.com/security-audit.html): every known finding, its GitHub ticket, and its real status, not a marketing page.
- [FAQ](https://traverse-framework.com/faq.html) and [Questions](https://traverse-framework.com/questions.html): 70+ specific Q&A pages, mostly long-tail but accurate.
- [What is exact-ref model execution?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-is-exact-ref-model-execution.html): discover → execute → trace; one shared `runtime.wasm`; signed schema `2.0.0` and later + `model.sig.json`; host-owned trust; **breaking** `model_usage` (`commercial` | `non_commercial`, else `usage_undeclared`); third-party ONNX via `traverse-cli model`; guest ABI v3 snapshot reuse; Core ML opt-in on Apple (macOS cargo test + Decision 113 spike; governed-path iPhone evidence for traverse#1630 shipped in v0.16.0); `digits-mlp-1.0.0` (test-only key; custody #1567 still open); published exact-ref execute is native + web 0.15.0 + Swift ExactModelHost (`swift-host-v0.15.0`) + Kotlin and .NET ExactModelHost in Maven/NuGet 0.15.0 (#1651 closed; first landed in v0.12.0); v0.16.0 republishes the same hosts at 0.16.0 and moves the execution policy to registration (#1706). No host is Certified. [Release](https://github.com/traverse-framework/traverse/releases/tag/v0.16.0) · historical embedder notes: [v0.14.0: what changed for embedders](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/traverse-0-14-0-what-changed-for-embedders.html).
- [How do hosts trust signed models?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-hosts-trust-signed-models.html): discover → execute → trace; one shared `runtime.wasm`; host-owned trust roots gate `register_package`; pin by digest + `model.sig.json`; `model_usage` required in v0.15.0; test-only digits-mlp key (custody #1567 still open); published exact-ref execute is native + web + Swift `swift-host-v0.15.0` + Kotlin and .NET 0.15.0; third-party ONNX can be packaged and signed with `traverse-cli model`.
- [Which hosts run signed exact-ref models?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/which-hosts-run-signed-exact-ref-models.html) · [Is production model signing ready?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/is-production-model-signing-ready.html) · [Can Kotlin or .NET run exact-ref yet?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/can-kotlin-or-dotnet-embedders-run-exact-ref-yet.html): discover → execute → trace; one shared `runtime.wasm`; published exact-ref on every host since 0.15.0; as of v0.17.1: native + web 0.17.1 + Swift asset `swift-host-v0.17.1` (`Package.swift` still pins `swift-host-v0.17.0`) + Kotlin and .NET 0.17.1 (#1651 closed); production signing custody is not finished (#1567 still open; v0.15.0 shipped key-generation tooling).
- [What is ExactModelHost?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-is-exact-model-host.html): host-side connector for governed exact-ref model packages (Spec 138). Register a signed package under host-owned trust roots, then execute under discover → execute → trace. Not a second runtime. Published since 0.15.0, current 0.17.1: native connector, web `ExactModelBrowserHost`, Swift `ExactModelHost` on asset `swift-host-v0.17.1` (`Package.swift` still pins `swift-host-v0.17.0`), Kotlin and .NET `ExactModelHost` in Maven/NuGet 0.17.1 (#1651 closed). Test-only digits-mlp key; custody #1567 still open. Not catalog `model.execute`. Not Hugging Face.
- [Signed models on every host. The rights travel with them.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/signed-models-on-every-host.html): Oct 15 v0.15.0 narrative. Discover → execute → trace; signed exact-ref on native Rust, web, Swift `swift-host-v0.15.0`, Kotlin and .NET 0.15.0 via small audited native boundaries sharing `traverse-model-host-frame`, byte-identical conformance vectors, one 21-case rights suite; **breaking** `model_usage`; `traverse-cli model` + `package-onnx` (install `traverse-cli-rs`, runner from `onnx-runner-v0.15.0`); ABI v3 prepare-once; Core ML opt-in on Apple (iPhone governed evidence traverse#1630 landed on main after the release, unreleased). Caveats: web `modelUsage` not validated in 0.15.0 (traverse#1685; fix #1698 on main, unreleased), CLI verify usage (traverse#1686, main only), test-only key (custody #1567), registry capability revocation #1598 not shipped. No host Certified.
- [What is model_usage?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-is-model-usage-in-traverse.html): since v0.15.0 apps with `exact_model_dependencies` must declare `model_usage: commercial | non_commercial` or fail closed with `usage_undeclared`; `commercial` rejects `prohibited` packages (`rights_policy_denied`); results carry `model_evidence`; Rust `ExactModelHostConnector::model_usage`, web `modelUsage`, Swift `modelUsage:` (no default), Kotlin/.NET `modelUsage`. 0.15.0 gaps fixed in v0.16.0: web 0.15.0 accepted any string (traverse#1685; `traverse-embedder-web@0.16.0` rejects with `usage_invalid`); `traverse-cli-rs` 0.15.0 `model verify` had no usage flag (traverse#1686; v0.16.0 adds `--model-usage` / `--require-model-usage`).
- [How do I package my own ONNX model?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-package-an-onnx-model-for-traverse.html): `cargo install traverse-cli-rs --version =0.17.1 --locked` (Rust ≥ 1.95; crates.io `traverse-cli` is unrelated) with `runner.wasm` from GitHub release `onnx-runner-v0.17.1` (sha256 `ac5591fac5f37435667169e969f9117cc6f81dc66b73cd74d1aef9000f5d3a0a`, `tract-onnx` 0.23.9; the v0.16.0, v0.16.1, and v0.16.2 runner releases carry the same bytes); the 0.15.0 CLI pairs with `onnx-runner-v0.15.0` (`f3902703…`); `model package-onnx` → sign → verify → conformance → pin; v0.16.0 adds named multi-input/multi-output packaging for HF-style text encoders (traverse#1661; reference package `hf-text-encoder-toy-1.0.0`), 0.15.0 is one input + one output tensor; post-processing belongs in capabilities, hosts stay UI + I/O. This is the host connector path, not Hugging Face.
- [What happens when a host marks a model package revoked?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-happens-when-a-host-marks-a-model-package-revoked.html): v0.15.0 hosts own a package-status map for signed model packages, `revoked` blocks (`package_revoked`), `deprecated` runs and is flagged; `model_evidence` on every result. Separate from registry capability revocation, which the runtime refuses since v0.16.0 (#1728).
- [Can Traverse run models on a GPU or the Apple Neural Engine?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/can-traverse-run-models-on-a-gpu-or-neural-engine.html): Core ML is an opt-in Apple placement in v0.15.0. Default stays `wasm-cpu`. Ordered placements, on-device self-check, fail-closed `placement_unavailable`, placement evidence (Decision 112). v0.15.0 evidence was macOS cargo test plus the Decision 113 iPhone spike. Governed-path iPhone evidence shipped in v0.16.0 (traverse#1630): BirdNET on one iPhone 14 Pro Max, p95 141 ms per 3 s clip under `[coreml, wasm-cpu]`; needs schema 2.3.0 `score_transform` (new in v0.16.0); `cpu_and_neural_engine` failed self-check and fell back to `wasm-cpu`; a Nov 3 rerun on main (#1778, docs only) shows `cpu_only` fails identically (5.067×10⁻³ vs 5×10⁻³ on 1 of 21 clips), so it is not Neural-Engine-specific. No web, Android, or desktop GPU adapter. No host is Certified.
- [How fast does a model run on iPhone with Traverse?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-fast-does-a-model-run-on-iphone-with-traverse.html): one measured case, shipped in v0.16.0 (traverse#1630, PR #1709): iPhone 14 Pro Max, iOS 26.6, Release build, Swift `ExactModelHost`, BirdNET v2.4 int8, policy `[coreml, wasm-cpu]`. Core ML `all` p95 141.3 ms per 3 s clip vs `wasm-cpu` p95 10.0 s; top-5 21/21 vs wasm-cpu; timing is the whole governed call. Not reproducible on v0.15.0 (needs schema 2.3.0 `score_transform`, new in v0.16.0). One device, one model, test-only key, non-commercial weights. Code for #1706 (placement prep at registration, Decision 120, #1764) and #1708 (self-check worst case, #1766) shipped in v0.16.0. Nov 3 rerun on main (#1778 docs, #1779 host tests; harness built from main `9a3cd84`): `cpu_only` registers 4.47 s, first call 4.29 s, no timeout, but runs on `wasm-cpu` (Core ML variant fails self-check); `all` p95 149.0 ms; different clips, not a before/after. #1706 and #1708 closed; #1707 open. No host is Certified.
- [How does a human approve an AI agent's plan in Traverse?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-does-a-human-approve-an-ai-agents-plan-in-traverse.html): on main, Spec 109 1.1.0 says a local CLI prompt mints a signed single-use token after a person confirms, and no MCP command can. A local page is deferred. That prompt is not in the tree. Stdio has no `approve` command (`SUPPORTING_COMMANDS` in `stdio_server.rs`; the command doc omits `search_capabilities`). `execute_proposal_via_mcp` denies with `approval_token_required`, `proposal_digest_mismatch`, `snapshot_digest_mismatch`, and `use_count_exhausted`. The verifier is already in v0.17.1. The spec text is not. Spec 113 FR-009/FR-010 describe a trace-bound remainder replan; `plan_workflow` does not implement it. Decision 136, #1897, #1930, #1896 closed 2026-11-23. Narrative: [The host is supposed to mint the token. MCP cannot.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/host-mints-the-token-mcp-cannot.html). Docs: [Spec 109](https://github.com/traverse-framework/traverse/blob/main/specs/109-runtime-workflow-proposals/spec.md), [workflow proposal lifecycle](https://github.com/traverse-framework/traverse/blob/main/docs/workflow-proposal-lifecycle.md).
- [How does a Traverse host prove which model it ran?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-does-a-traverse-host-prove-which-model-it-ran.html): on npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.17.1`, `execute` returns `model_evidence` (and `trace.model_evidence`) after re-hashing the cached manifest and guest. `digest` is the manifest SHA-256. `modelRightsRecord` can show `revoked` without a run. A revoked execute is `package_revoked`. Spec 138 0.8.0, Decision 107, since v0.15.0. Not a signature over the output. Narrative: [The host result names the model it ran](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/host-result-names-the-model-it-ran.html). Docs: [exact-ref model execution](https://github.com/traverse-framework/traverse/blob/v0.17.1/docs/exact-ref-model-execution.md), [model-rights-record-1.0.0](https://github.com/traverse-framework/traverse/blob/v0.17.1/contracts/connectors/traverse.model-runtime/schemas/model-rights-record-1.0.0.json).
- [How do I read the model output frame on a native Traverse host?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-read-the-model-output-frame-on-a-native-traverse-host.html): on crates.io `traverse-runtime` 0.17.1, `ExactModelMediatedConnector::activated()` keeps an `Arc` so `with_host_mut` can read `output_ref` after `model.execute`. `activate_exact_model_runtime` still takes the host by value. Changelog #1785, PR #1809. On npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.17.1`, `host.io.readModelOutput(result.output_ref, maxBytes)`. A missing ref is `unavailable`. Swift, Android, and .NET mediated activation is not in v0.17.1. Docs: [host connector command dispatch](https://github.com/traverse-framework/traverse/blob/v0.17.1/docs/host-connector-command-dispatch.md).
- [How do I publish a new version of a signed Traverse model?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-publish-a-new-version-of-a-signed-traverse-model.html): a new model is a new manifest, signature, and digest. The runtime does not follow a version range or substitute a file during execute. Registration fails `pin_mismatch` unless `exact_model_dependencies` names the new digest. The old pin still names the old bytes. `setPackageStatus` replaces the host map: `deprecated` still runs and `model_evidence.status` is `deprecated`; `revoked` fails `package_revoked`. A status change drops the ABI v3 snapshot. Verify with `traverse-cli model verify` (`cargo install traverse-cli-rs`, binary `traverse-cli`) before register. Docs: [exact-ref model execution](https://github.com/traverse-framework/traverse/blob/v0.17.1/docs/exact-ref-model-execution.md).
- [How does Traverse choose a model dependency in the browser?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-does-traverse-choose-a-model-dependency-in-the-browser.html): on npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.17.1`, call `resolveBrowserModelDependency` with the Spec 045 dependency, `requested_placement` `browser`, and the activated pins. `ollama.local.generate` is `model_provider_unavailable` with no HTTP probe. An activated `exact-ref.wasm-cpu` pin is selected with `trust_class` `verified_signed_package`. If none remain, `failure_code` is `model_dependency_unsatisfied` and `trust_class` is absent. `exactRefPinFromSelected` returns `model_id` and `version`. The resolver file also matches npm `@0.17.0`. Decision 95, #1835, #1843. Narrative: [The browser skips Ollama and picks a signed model pin](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/browser-skips-ollama-picks-signed-pin.html). Docs: [Spec 045](https://github.com/traverse-framework/traverse/blob/v0.17.1/specs/045-governed-model-dependency-resolution/spec.md).
- [How does the same signed model package run on every Traverse host?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-does-the-same-signed-model-package-run-on-every-traverse-host.html): register the same three files (`model.manifest.json`, `model.wasm`, `model.sig.json`) on each host. The pin is the SHA-256 of the exact manifest bytes. On `wasm-cpu`, a host that supports that schema and ABI returns the same output bytes for the same frame (`model conformance check` on `wasmtime` and `wasmi`). Native `ExactModelHostConnector` and browser `ExactModelBrowserHost` match the checked-in vector; the digits vector is also byte-identical on Swift. Core ML uses the variant tolerance. v0.17.1 native hosts read the frame after `model.execute` through `ExactModelMediatedConnector::activated()` (#1785). Product packages: crates.io `traverse-runtime` 0.17.1, npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.17.1`, Maven and NuGet 0.17.1; the v0.17.1 README lists the iOS/macOS binary as `swift-host-v0.17.0`. `ExactModelHost` ships in every embedder as of 0.15.0. ABI v3 needs 0.15.0 or later. No host is Certified. Docs: [model packaging guide](https://github.com/traverse-framework/traverse/blob/v0.17.1/docs/model-packaging-guide.md), [exact-ref model execution](https://github.com/traverse-framework/traverse/blob/v0.17.1/docs/exact-ref-model-execution.md).
- [How do I verify a Traverse model package signature before I run it?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-verify-a-traverse-model-package-signature.html): `cargo +1.95.0 install traverse-cli-rs --version =0.17.1 --locked` (binary `traverse-cli`; crates.io `traverse-cli` is unrelated), then `traverse-cli model verify <package-dir> --trusted-key <public-key-hex> --model-usage commercial|non_commercial --json`. Checks the detached Ed25519 `model.sig.json`, the key, manifest, rights (including derivation), WASM digest, target, ceilings, and zero imports. Exits non-zero on failure (`signature_invalid`, `key_untrusted`, `digest_mismatch`, `rights_incomplete`, `rights_inconsistent`, `manifest_invalid`, `host_limit_exceeded`). Without `--model-usage`, `verification_usage` stays `non_commercial` and `effective_usage` is null. `--require-model-usage` alone reproduces `usage_undeclared`. `--json` usage errors are `error.code` `usage_error`, exit 5. The host repeats the checks at `register_package` / `registerPackage` and re-hashes on execute. At tag v0.17.1, `TRAVERSE_MODEL_SIGNING_KEYS` is empty in `traverse-runtime` and `traverse-embedder-web`, and `keys/model-signing/` has no `.pub` file. `digits-mlp-1.0.0` in that tag uses the test-only key. Production procedure: [ADR-0080](https://github.com/traverse-framework/traverse/blob/v0.17.1/docs/adr/0080-model-signing-key-management.md) and the [model-signing key runbook](https://github.com/traverse-framework/traverse/blob/v0.17.1/docs/model-signing-key-runbook.md). Capability `signature.json` is a different check.
- [How does Traverse check that a host can run a compatible capability?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-does-traverse-check-that-a-host-can-run-a-compatible-capability.html): on v0.17.1, `runtime.wasm` starts a compatible capability only when `host_platform` is in `platforms` (Spec 072 1.1.0 FR-010 and FR-011). The init header is `execution_mode: compatible`, a non-empty `platforms` list, and `host_platform`, with no artifact bytes. A miss is `platform_not_supported` (`invalid_state`, status `-1`) and emits no event. `traverse_contracts::CompatibleLifecycle` canonicalizes input first (`input_not_canonicalizable`), then does the membership check. Web (`traverse-embedder-web@0.17.1`) rejects an empty `platforms` list at load and sends `config.platform`, or `web` when omitted. Instance ids are `{capability_id}-compatible-{n}`. v0.16.2 still returns `-1` from the compatible exports. Use `runtime-wasm-v0.17.1`. No host is Certified. Docs: [Spec 072](https://github.com/traverse-framework/traverse/blob/v0.17.1/specs/072-native-bridge-compatible-lifecycle/spec.md).
- [How do I cancel a running model.execute call in Traverse?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-cancel-a-running-model-execute-call-in-traverse.html): on npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.17.1`, pass an `AbortSignal` to `ExactModelBrowserHost.execute` and call `abort()`. A browser Worker is terminated mid-run (`cancelled`). On crates.io `traverse-runtime` 0.17.1, set `ExactModelHostConnector.cancel` while `invoke` runs; wasmtime stops at the next epoch check. Reset the flag yourself. Node and `createWorker: null` report `cancelled` after the guest returns. Narrative: [Stop a model.execute call while it is still running](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/stop-a-model-call-mid-run.html). Docs: [exact-ref model execution](https://github.com/traverse-framework/traverse/blob/v0.17.1/docs/exact-ref-model-execution.md).
- [How do I set a deadline on a Traverse model call?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-set-a-deadline-on-a-traverse-model-call.html): pass `timeout_ms` on `execute` (`traverse-embedder-web@0.17.1`) or on the `model.execute` payload (`traverse-runtime` 0.17.1). The host uses the smaller of `timeout_ms` and the manifest `max_execution_ms`. A browser Worker and wasmtime fail with `timeout` during the call. Node checks before the call and after the guest returns. `registerPackage` `preparationBudgetMs` is capped by `maxPreparationMs` (default five minutes); aborting its `signal` fails `cancelled` and keeps nothing. Narrative: [Stop a model.execute call while it is still running](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/stop-a-model-call-mid-run.html). Docs: [exact-ref model execution](https://github.com/traverse-framework/traverse/blob/v0.17.1/docs/exact-ref-model-execution.md).
- [What is the model.execute catalog capability?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-is-the-model-execute-catalog-capability.html): `model.execute@1.0.0` in the registry catalog (registry#639, index-v407, Oct 15 2026). A shim over host connector `traverse.model-runtime`: exact pin + `input_ref` + `model_usage` + non-empty `trust_root` in; `model_evidence` or unchanged fail-closed Spec 138 reason out. Does not fetch models, hold keys, or choose a model. Pins connector 2.3.0 (shipped in Traverse v0.16.0; v0.15.0 hosts carry 2.2.0). Registry spec 027 is draft. Since Traverse v0.16.1 (Nov 3) it runs on published native, Node and browser packages: traverse#1770 shipped web `activateMediatedConnector` + `submitAsync`, and a published-package run (traverse#1782, clean-runner CI #1783) gave identical output and six identical fail-closed reasons on native, Node and Chromium; Swift/Android/.NET activation not shipped; the Oct 16 weekly demo runs it on v0.15.0 via a native bridge and labelled Browser/Node glue.
- [Does catalog model.execute run on published Traverse packages?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/does-catalog-model-execute-run-on-published-traverse-packages.html): yes on native, Node and browser since v0.16.1 (Nov 3, 2026). Published `model.execute@1.0.0` guest, unchanged, over signed `traverse.digits-onnx@1.0.0` (test-only key): crates.io `traverse-runtime` 0.16.1 (wasmtime), npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.16.1` in Node 24 and Chromium. `all_identical: true`: success output, 56-byte frame, and `connector_unavailable`/`usage_undeclared`/`key_untrusted`/`pin_mismatch`/`digest_mismatch`/`package_revoked` (native adds `placement_evidence`). Evidence traverse#1782; clean GitHub-hosted runner CI #1783 (pinned to v0.16.1). Limits: `runtime.wasm` came from the tag at run time (now also on `runtime-wasm-v0.16.1`; #1784 closed), native frame read-back needs a workaround on v0.16.2 (#1785, fixed in v0.17.1 by #1809), no Swift/Android/.NET activation, registry spec 027 draft, no host Certified.
- [Where does BundleEmbedder get runtime.wasm?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/where-does-bundleembedder-get-runtime-wasm.html): from the app bundle (`runtime/runtime.wasm` + `.sha256`, digest-checked, fail closed if missing). npm does not ship it. Current match for npm 0.17.1 is `runtime-wasm-v0.17.1` (sha256 `f2b1bebe…`, bridge 1.1.0). Since Nov 4, 2026 it is also on artifact-only GitHub releases `runtime-wasm-v0.16.2` (sha256 `b313b5c5…`) and `runtime-wasm-v0.16.1` (`7a322a17…`), with `runtime.wasm.sha256` and `runtime-release.json`; take the one matching your `traverse-embedder-web` version and check the digest. traverse#1784 closed by #1797; on main, every future `vX.Y.Z` tag publishes `runtime-wasm-vX.Y.Z` before the product release.
- [Can a Traverse application manifest invoke a host connector?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/can-a-traverse-application-manifest-invoke-a-host-connector.html): yes since v0.16.2 (Nov 4, 2026). A state invokes exactly one of `{"capability_id", "input_from"}` or `{"host_connector": "audio.permission.request"}`; `traverse-cli app validate`, activation and registration accept both (Spec 1773, #1772). Neither, both, empty or unknown fields fail closed; host-connector states must route `host_connector_succeeded`/`failed`/`timeout`/`cancelled`; the command must be declared and resolve through Specs 104/137. Limit on v0.16.2: `traverse-cli app activate` registered only its built-in reference connector catalog without `traverse.audio-input` (#1791); registration shipped in v0.17.1 via #1796 (Nov 5). On 0.16.2 the limit remains.
- [What input does a runtime.wasm guest receive?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-input-does-a-runtime-wasm-guest-receive.html): on published v0.16.2 and earlier, Swift/Kotlin/.NET guests see the whole `{target_id, input}` envelope; on main (#1800, Nov 5, closing #1794) `runtime.wasm` unwraps it and gives the guest only canonical `input` (Spec 1722), rejecting wrong `target_id` (`target_not_found`), bad input, and extra members (`ambiguous_submit`). Raw web submits unchanged unless both keys are present. Breaking for envelope-reading guests; none in-repo. Related web raw-submit `kind:app_command` routing fixed on main (#1802 via #1806). Shipped in v0.17.1.
- [Who owns the compatible-capability lifecycle?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/who-owns-the-compatible-capability-lifecycle.html): Decision 127: `runtime.wasm` owns compatible start/stop/kill, instance ids, events, Spec 1722 start input, and the `platforms[]` allowlist on every host including web. On traverse main: #1822 (runtime + Spec 072 1.1.0) and #1824 (Swift, Kotlin, .NET, web switch; Decision 128) merged Nov 6. Rust embedder moved onto the same shared rules and codes under Decision 129 (#1828, merged Nov 9); Rust submit takes raw JSON text (#1829). Published v0.16.2 still stubs those exports to `-1`; web still has a TypeScript lifecycle. Shipped in v0.17.1.
- [What errors does a web compatible capability return?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-errors-does-a-web-compatible-capability-return.html): On traverse main since #1824 (Decision 128), web passes runtime.wasm codes through: `compatible_instance_active`, `compatible_instance_not_active` (replaces `instance_not_found` / `instance_not_running`), `input_not_canonicalizable`, `invalid_input`, `platform_not_supported`; one instance per capability at a time. Breaking for web callers. Published traverse-embedder-web 0.16.2 unchanged. Shipped in v0.17.1.
- [Why does BundleEmbedder fail with "cannot find definition for import (traverse_host, connector_invoke)"?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/why-does-bundleembedder-fail-with-cannot-find-definition-for-import-connector-invoke.html): published browser/Node `runtime.wasm` (traverse-embedder-web 0.15.0) doesn't link the Spec 104 `connector_invoke` import; only native wasmtime does, with a host-written `MediatedConnector` bridge. Partly fixed in v0.16.0 (Nov 2): traverse#1755 links `connector_invoke` in `runtime.wasm` with native-parity fail-closed mediation (without host activation, invokes get `unbound`/`undeclared` with evidence) and ships native `ExactModelMediatedConnector` / `activate_exact_model_runtime` (no hand-written bridge); in published packages web/Swift/Android/.NET still have no activation API. Shipped in v0.16.1 (Nov 3, traverse-embedder-web@0.16.1): traverse#1770 adds web `BundleEmbedder.activateMediatedConnector` + `exactModelMediatedConnector`, guest suspend/resume at `connector_invoke`, `submitAsync` (sync `submit` -> `async_submit_required`), and a host-private filter fix for rights-record URLs in `model_evidence`; run on published packages in Node and Chromium (traverse#1782). traverse#1719 closed; Swift/Android/.NET activation still open.
- [Why does model.execute return unauthorized_output?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/why-does-model-execute-return-unauthorized-output.html): the Spec 104 host-private filter rejects strings starting with `/` or containing `://`; the full `ModelRightsRecord` carries `source_url`, so don't forward it. `model.execute@1.1.0` (registry#641 closed via #645, 2026-10-29; same WASM digest as 1.0.0) defines the normative flat `model_evidence` (`license_id`, `commercial_use`, `status`, `effective_usage`, optional URL-free `derivation`); full nested record is non-conformant. Shipped host binding still open (traverse#1719).
- [Does the same Traverse WASM give byte-identical output on every host?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/does-the-same-wasm-give-byte-identical-output-on-every-host.html): same WASM + same input bytes → same output bytes, but on v0.15.0 hosts don't always pass the same bytes: `traverse-mcp` re-serializes request JSON with sorted keys, embedders pass caller bytes through, so catalog `core.authorize@1.2.0` gives the same decision/reason/obligations/trace but a different `policy_hash` (`2a126b86…` vs `51a64653…`). Sorted-key input → byte-identical on all three. Fixed in v0.16.0 (Nov 2, breaking): Decision 118 + Spec `1722-canonical-guest-input-bytes`. Every host feeds guests RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON input; unrepresentable input → `input_not_canonicalizable`; outputs never rewritten; conformance fixture `fixtures/cross-host/canonical-input-v1` on native, `runtime.wasm`, Node (traverse#1739, merged Oct 28). v0.15.0 keeps the old behavior. Write-up: [Same WASM, two hashes](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/same-wasm-two-hashes.html). Demo rerun on `main` before the tag (Browser + Node + traverse-mcp all `51a64653…`): [One audit fingerprint, every host](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/hash-converges.html). Rerun Nov 3 on released bits, Node (npm 0.16.0) + `traverse-mcp-v0.16.0` binary → both `51a64653…`, full output byte-identical; browser not rerun: [Traverse v0.16.0: same input, same output](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/traverse-0-16-0-same-input-same-output.html).
- [What is digits-mlp?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-is-digits-mlp.html): first trained exact-ref package in v0.14.0 (UCI digits MLP, 96.10% held-out, bit-identical); test-only signing; not a general LLM.
- [Does the website use the latest traverse-embedder-web?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/does-the-website-use-the-latest-traverse-embedder.html): site still pins `^0.16.2` (npm is 0.17.1; the site has not moved, checked 2026-11-16) and `/discover` admits its signed demo fixture through `registerPackage` with an execution policy and `modelUsage: non_commercial`; the `/discover` execute panel ships its own `runtime.wasm`, the `runtime-wasm-v0.16.2` release asset (`b313b5c5…`, updated Nov 5 from the v0.13.0 copy); the site can lag future releases, so product apps pin published packages, not the website demo.
- [How does Traverse complement Hugging Face?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-does-traverse-complement-hugging-face.html): Hub = provenance; Traverse = pinned signed client-first capability; not Transformers.js/Hub replacement; no defer promise until a second executor exists.
